episode.title: Recover a reasoning-only incomplete-response stall by handing the turn to a fallback
episode.before: At parent d45fd1aa31e54e411a0df2661849ccb255c22ed6, incomplete responses shared one aggregate retry counter. After three continuation attempts, a response containing no visible answer or tool call was persisted and returned as a terminal partial result. The loop did not distinguish a consecutive reasoning-only stall, invoke configured failover for that condition, reserve a call for the fallback when the iteration budget was exhausted, or remove protocol-specific continuation state when crossing to another request protocol.
episode.after: At 656eb283096c979ae4e6dc454920c2038e622990, the turn maintains a separately reset consecutive reasoning-only streak. A response with neither visible content nor tool calls increments that streak, while visible progress resets it. On the third consecutive reasoning-only incomplete response, the runtime attempts configured failover using the semantic reason incomplete_response, resets incomplete counters, grants exactly one budget grace call if needed, re-synchronizes the cached system identity, and continues the same turn. When the fallback uses a different protocol, request assembly removes the source protocol's synthetic nudge and opaque reasoning-only rows from the outbound copy while retaining session history and valid role alternation. If no fallback can be activated, the existing terminal partial-result behavior remains.
episode.diff: The merge adds an incomplete_response failover reason and per-turn reasoning-only streak state; extends incomplete-response handling to detect three consecutive no-answer/no-tool responses, activate fallback, and reserve a bounded grace iteration; propagates a fallback-activated verdict through response intake so system identity is rebuilt; and extends outbound transcript normalization to discard the source-only continuation nudge during cross-protocol handoff. Focused tests cover successful fallback after three stalls, exactly one grace call, streak reset after visible partial progress, and removal of incompatible replay/nudge state from the fallback wire.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned resolution is merge commit 656eb283096c979ae4e6dc454920c2038e622990 with first parent d45fd1aa31e54e411a0df2661849ccb255c22ed6; its subject states that reasoning-only stalls switch to a fallback instead of ending incomplete.

Before the change, continue_codex_incomplete used only _codex_incomplete_retries and returned a terminal partial result after the third attempt; it had no consecutive reasoning-only predicate or failover branch.
The new implementation defines reasoning-only as absent visible content and absent tool calls, increments a consecutive streak only for that state, and resets the streak otherwise.

On the third consecutive reasoning-only response, the handler attempts fallback with FailoverReason.incomplete_response; successful activation resets both counters, records the current session messages, and returns a distinct fallback-activated verdict. Failure to activate a fallback falls through to the prior terminal sentinel.

If the stall trigger has consumed either the call-count or iteration budget, the handler sets _budget_grace_call so the activated fallback can be invoked, while resetting the streak makes repeated grace allocation through the same stall unreachable.

The reasoning-only streak is initialized with other per-turn recovery state and is also reset after a normal non-incomplete response or terminal incomplete handling, preventing state leakage across successful responses and turns.

Response intake recognizes the fallback-activated verdict, re-synchronizes the cached system prompt with the newly selected model/provider identity, and returns continue so the main conversation loop builds another request rather than terminating the turn.

For a request crossing away from the source response protocol, request assembly drops thinking-only/replay rows and the exact synthetic continuation marker from the API-copy transcript, then merges adjacent user messages to preserve role alternation without mutating stored history.

The focused end-to-end test supplies three reasoning-only incomplete responses followed by a fallback answer and asserts completed output, failover reason incomplete_response, four total API calls, and consumption of the single grace flag.

A focused test places visible partial progress before three reasoning-only responses and asserts that recovery still occurs only after the subsequent consecutive stall sequence, exercising streak reset independently from the aggregate incomplete count.

The cross-protocol test records every outbound request and asserts that the fallback request contains neither the synthetic continuation nudge nor opaque reasoning items and that non-system roles alternate.
The change adds incomplete_response to the typed failover-reason enumeration and updates its enumeration test, making the new recovery cause part of the existing failover contract.

Focused runtime tests could not be executed in the pinned detached worktree because the available Python installation does not contain pytest; validation is therefore limited to direct inspection of the committed test oracles and call paths.

candidate_atomics.name: detect-consecutive-nonproductive-responses
candidate_atomics.title: Detect a consecutive no-answer response stall
candidate_atomics.description: Track a local consecutive streak for incomplete responses that contain neither visible answer text nor a tool call, resetting it when observable progress occurs so nonconsecutive failures do not trigger recovery.

semantic_action.intent: Distinguish a persistent nonproductive response loop from ordinary incomplete responses that make visible progress.
semantic_action.pre_state: The turn receives an incomplete response and already maintains aggregate continuation accounting, but consecutive responses with no visible answer or tool call are not independently represented.
semantic_action.post_state: Each incomplete response has updated consecutive-stall state: a no-answer/no-tool response increments the streak, while observable progress resets it; the state is reset at normal completion and turn boundaries.
semantic_action.validation: Drive a visible partial followed by three reasoning-only incomplete responses and verify that failover occurs only after the three consecutive nonproductive responses.

candidate_atomics.name: handoff-stalled-turn-with-bounded-budget
candidate_atomics.title: Hand a persistently stalled turn to a fallback with one bounded call
candidate_atomics.description: After the configured consecutive-stall threshold, activate the existing fallback chain with a typed failure reason and reserve one call when the ordinary turn budget has already been consumed.

semantic_action.intent: Recover a live turn that repeatedly produces no usable answer instead of terminating it as an incomplete partial result before a fallback is tried.
semantic_action.pre_state: The consecutive no-answer response threshold has been reached during an incomplete turn, and a configured fallback may be available; the triggering response may have consumed the remaining iteration budget.
semantic_action.post_state: If fallback activation succeeds, recovery counters are reset, the same turn continues under the fallback identity, and at most one budget-grace call permits the fallback request. If no fallback is available, the existing terminal partial-result path remains in force.
semantic_action.validation: Supply three consecutive reasoning-only responses at a three-call budget followed by a successful fallback response; assert the typed failover reason, completed answer, exactly four calls, and a consumed grace flag.

candidate_atomics.name: sanitize-transcript-for-protocol-handoff
candidate_atomics.title: Remove source-only continuation state before a protocol handoff
candidate_atomics.description: Build the fallback request from a copy of conversation history that excludes the prior protocol's synthetic continuation instruction and opaque reasoning replay state while restoring valid role alternation.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent protocol-specific recovery artifacts from leaking into a fallback request that cannot interpret them.
semantic_action.module_role: Outbound conversation projection and protocol adapter
semantic_action.pre_state: Fallback activation changes the request protocol while stored session history contains thinking-only replay rows and a synthetic continuation marker used by the prior protocol.
semantic_action.post_state: The outbound fallback request excludes the incompatible marker and replay state, adjacent user rows are reconciled to preserve role alternation, and canonical stored session history remains available unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Capture the fallback wire request after a three-response stall and assert absence of the marker and opaque reasoning items plus alternating non-system roles.

candidate_workflows.name: recover-consecutive-no-answer-response-stall
candidate_workflows.title: Recover a turn stuck producing internal reasoning without an answer
candidate_workflows.description: Detect consecutive incomplete responses with no user-visible progress, escalate the live turn through the configured fallback chain with a strictly bounded budget exception, and adapt the transcript if the fallback speaks a different request protocol.

workflow_graph.goal: Complete the same user turn through a configured fallback when repeated incomplete responses contain neither an answer nor a tool call, without allowing unbounded retries or leaking source-protocol control state.
when_to_use: A response API repeatedly returns an incomplete status while exposing no visible answer text and no tool call.
The runtime has an existing fallback chain capable of continuing the same turn.
Continuation replay or a synthetic nudge has already failed to produce observable progress.
anti_goals: Do not classify visible partial progress as part of an uninterrupted no-answer streak.
Do not grant an open-ended iteration-budget extension or repeatedly allocate grace calls.
Do not mutate canonical conversation history solely to satisfy the fallback protocol.
Do not send source-protocol continuation markers or opaque replay state to an incompatible destination.
Do not replace the existing terminal partial-result behavior when no fallback can be activated.
not_applicable_when: The response contains visible answer content or a tool call and therefore demonstrates progress.
The failure is a transport exception, policy refusal, malformed request, or another condition already represented by a different recovery reason.
No fallback is configured or permitted and the caller requires immediate terminal handling.
The destination uses the same protocol and can safely consume the existing replay and continuation state.
inputs: Normalized response status, visible content, and tool-call fields
Per-turn consecutive-stall and aggregate incomplete counters
Configured fallback chain and typed recovery reason
API call count and remaining iteration budget
Current request protocol and fallback request protocol
Canonical session messages and active system identity
workflow_graph.entry_state: A live turn has received an incomplete response; continuation state and aggregate retry accounting exist, but the runtime must determine whether this response extends a consecutive no-answer stall.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Either a configured fallback has received a protocol-compatible request and produced a normal turn result using no more than one bounded grace call, or fallback activation was unavailable and the established terminal partial-result path handled the turn.

steps.condition: For every incomplete response in the active turn.
steps.validation: The streak increments only when both visible content and tool calls are absent, and resets on visible progress or a normal response.

steps.condition: The consecutive-stall threshold is reached and the configured fallback chain can activate; otherwise retain terminal partial handling.
steps.validation: The fallback receives incomplete_response, the same turn continues, and an exhausted normal budget yields exactly one additional request opportunity.

steps.condition: Fallback activation changes to a protocol that must not receive the source protocol's continuation marker or opaque reasoning replay state.
steps.validation: The fallback wire excludes incompatible recovery artifacts and retains valid role alternation, while stored session history remains intact.

validation_ladder: Unit-level state oracle: visible progress resets the local stall streak independently of aggregate incomplete-response accounting.
Recovery integration oracle: three consecutive no-answer responses invoke the typed fallback reason and produce the fallback's completed answer.
Budget oracle: a stall that consumes the normal three-call budget produces exactly one fallback grace call and leaves the grace flag consumed.
Protocol-handoff oracle: the fallback wire contains neither source-only continuation text nor opaque reasoning replay state and preserves alternating non-system roles.

Regression oracle: when fallback activation fails, terminal partial-result behavior remains available; this branch is supported by implementation inspection but has no new focused test in the changed test file.
stop_conditions: Stop retrying through this workflow once a normal response supplies visible content or a tool call.
Stop after the fallback consumes the single grace request; do not allocate another grace call for the same stall.
Stop escalation and use the existing terminal partial result when no fallback can be activated.
Defer promotion if the runtime cannot reliably distinguish visible output and tool calls or lacks a configured fallback mechanism.
unresolved_or_deferred: The committed tests could not be executed in the available environment because pytest is not installed.
The changed focused tests do not directly exercise the no-fallback terminal branch, although the implementation explicitly retains it.
GitHub discussion, review rationale, and status-check results are unavailable in the supplied evidence bundle.

unresolved_questions: Were the focused tests and broader agent suite successful in CI? The supplied GitHub bundle omits status checks, and local execution was blocked by the missing pytest package.

Is three consecutive nonproductive responses a deliberately configurable policy boundary or a fixed implementation choice? The inspected change hard-codes the threshold and provides no available review discussion.
No cross-project Resolution Pattern is proposed: this extraction contains only one repository Workflow and therefore cannot satisfy the meta-skill's multi-repository promotion gate.
